uncited: - **Inputs**: $\text{MSE}_{\text{full}}$ (Mean Squared Error of the full method), $\text{MSE}_{\text{config}}$ (Mean Squared Error of the ablated configuration).
- No specific data structures are required; the metric operates on scalar MSE values derived from image comparisons.
Calculate the PSNR for the full method: $\text{PSNR}_{\text{full}} = 10 \log_{10} \frac{\text{MAX}^2}{\text{MSE}_{\text{full}}}$.
Calculate the PSNR for the ablated configuration: $\text{PSNR}_{\text{config}} = 10 \log_{10} \frac{\text{MAX}^2}{\text{MSE}_{\text{config}}}$.
Compute the difference $\Delta$ by subtracting the two PSNR values.
- **Division by Zero**: If $\text{MSE}_{\text{config}}$ is zero, the logarithm is undefined.
- **Sign Interpretation**: A positive $\Delta$ indicates the ablated method has higher error (worse quality) than the full method.
- **Time Complexity**: $O(1)$ for the calculation itself, assuming MSE values are precomputed.
The metric is derived from the properties of the logarithmic scale used in PSNR calculations.
